- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid excessive sell-off bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to align with volatility decay.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.3), model frequently underestimates upward momentum; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next 5–7 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile; apply +0.5–1.0% bias to short-term forecasts.
- When sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often lags; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and apply +0.5–1.5% upward bias to align with sentiment shift.
- In high volatility periods (e.g., sentiment swings >0.3), model overfits recent noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before applying sentiment-weighted adjustment.
